label: Dionysius of Corinth wrote to the church at Amastris and the churches of Pontus, naming bishop Palmas

date.note: Same letter-collection as lit-dionysius-nicomedia: Dionysius of Corinth wrote during Soter's Roman episcopate (c. 166-174). Harnack notes that at Amastris 'the metropolitan organization was in working order by the reign of M. Aurelius,' the bishop Palmas presiding over the Pontic churches.

primary.cite: Dionysius of Corinth, Letter to the church at Amastris and the churches in Pontus (naming bishop Palmas; requested by Bacchylides and Elpistus), in Eusebius, Hist. eccl. 4.23.6

secondary.cite: Harnack, Mission and Expansion, vol. 2, p. 188; synopsis at p. 95

notes: Eusebius (HE 4.23.6) preserves that Dionysius wrote 'to the church sojourning at Amastris together with those in Pontus,' mentioning their bishop Palmas by name. A contemporary attestation of an organized, senior see at Amastris (844856, mod. Amasra) c. 170. 1 Peter and Pliny attest Christians in Pontus only as a province; here Dionysius names a city, and the Greek calls it the church paroikousa Amastrin, sojourning at Amastris.
